WHAT: produce a measured outcome for this surface on real traffic or a controlled live experiment you build (fresh omp sessions, real prompts or commands cut from session files). If the data does not exist, create it. UNMEASURED / NOT_RUN is never an acceptable close.
ACCEPTANCE: (1) a bar committed in a bead comment BEFORE outcome data is read; (2) the number with its denominator and a 95% interval where it is a rate; (3) spend stated; (4) a planted negative; (5) on a FAIL, LOSS DEPTH (autopsy, 3 one-variable hypotheses, dev replay, one held-out retest) before parking; (6) update work/jev-inventory/expected.json with the new verdict and re-bless the golden. title: pre-commit AUTOFIX_REFUSED tells agents to run autofix --staged, which rewrites and re-stages sibling files: 3 sweeps on 2026-09-25
description:
WHAT: githooks/pre-commit lane 2 (lines 131-135) prints the remedy '<autofix> --staged --repo <repo>' then 'git add -- <the rewritten paths>'. Add a gate witness: a scratch repo where a sibling file is staged and unclean, a path-limited commit of another unclean file is refused, and the printed remedy names only the committing path.

description: WHAT: A keyless checker, scripts/bar-reachable.py, that reads a prereg's arms from committed baseline/floor rows and computes the best achievable test result for the stated bar before any call. For paired McNemar: the maximum discordant pairs given the oracle headroom over the comparator on the exact prereg keys, and the smallest attainable p. WHY: jev-jjwt's prereg (c0ef4468) passed size and offered-answer feasibility, but its McNemar bar was unreachable (best single 22/24, max 2 discordant, p >= 0.5). comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: NON-AUTHOR CHECK (pane 1) of 6e4ff307: tests OK in a clean clone; plant max_wins = tasks (drop comparator subtraction) -> 2 tests FAIL, restored byte-identical (cmp). One fail-open gap, not closed: mcnemar_reachability sets max_discordant_wins = tasks - comparator_exact (bar-reachable.py:147), which assumes Jev can complete every task the comparator misses. For a choice over fixed candidates (Best-of-N) the ceiling is the tasks where some offered candidate completes and the comparator does not (oracle headroom). Without it the gate says REACHABLE when no offered option can win. Fix: optional --oracle-exact (or per-task oracle rows) capping max wins at oracle_exact - both_exact, plus a test built from floor_receipt.json where the tasks minus comparator count exceeds the oracle headroom. Resume after the planning duel.

title: Keyless autopsy: why Jev scores 65.8% on Climate-FEVER vs 90.2% on SciFact with the same verify design
description: WHAT: jev-oioo's Jev arm (work/jev-oioo/live-results.jsonl, 907 rows, jev-1.13.0, raw noul stored) got 597/907 = 65.8%, Brier 0.233, against 90.2% on SciFact. Error analysis per AGENTS.md loss-depth step 1 (skill://error-discovery): sample failures across SUPPORTS and REFUTES, split by class (confusion matrix, noul histogram per gold class), and name each failure mode with counts: missing evidence in the state (five sentences that do not all bear on the claim; Climate-FEVER per-sentence labels include NOT_ENOUGH_INFO), question design (the SciFact Noul wording asks 'supports'; REFUTES vs merely-not-supporting), label noise (claim_label vs sentence votes), harness bug, model limit. Use the local states under var/agent-tmp/jev-oioo (no raw text committed). Output: 3-5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses, each naming one variable, for a dev-slice replay. No live calls. WHY: a loss after one design is about the design until autopsied. ACCEPTANCE: committed autopsy note with counts and hash-keyed examples, ranked hypotheses; non-author check.
close_reason: VERDICT (non-author pane 1) at f025dd97: autopsy holds; counts reproduce except for one runner deviation I found while recounting. Confusion from live-results.jsonl with the MEASURED rule (noul > 0.5, work/noul-scifact/score.py and kit/src/verify.ts): SUPPORTS 348/654 correct, REFUTES 244/253, total 592/907 = 65.3%. The receipt and autopsy say 353 and 597 because work/jev-oioo/live.mjs:69 labels supported when noul >= 0.5; 5 rows sit exactly at 0.5. Filed on jev-oioo. Findings stand: errors are almost all SUPPORTS false negatives (306 of 315); 815/907 states carry heterogeneous or NOT_ENOUGH_INFO evidence; on the 92 clean states Jev still misses 22 SUPPORTS; harness 0 errors. Hypotheses ranked with one variable each; H1 (keep only evidence sentences that agree with the claim label) is next on a dev slice, never the held-out set.

title: Arm sanity check: compare a live arm's action-type mix with its reference arm after the first rows, and stop degenerate arms early
description:
WHAT: scripts/arm-sanity.py --arm <decisions.jsonl> --reference <decisions.jsonl> [--min-rows 200]. Classifies each decision's chosen action into a type (PokéJev: switch / move / tera, from the chosen string; MiniWoB: the verb before '[' such as click / type / select / none) and, among decisions where more than one type was offered, prints the per-type choice rate for both files, the absolute difference, and a two-proportion z. Exit 1 when any type's rate differs by more than --max-diff (default 0.25) with |z| > 4, or when one type takes >= 0.95 of choices while the reference is <= 0.80; exit 0 otherwise; exit 2 NOT_RUN when either file has fewer than --min-rows eligible decisions. Keyless, stdlib only.

WHY: 2026-09-25 three live arms ran on broken harnesses and the win or success rate alone did not say why: PokéJev leaf r2 switched on 99% of offered turns (reference 41%), r3 on 99.5%, MiniWoB v3 isolated arms typed 0 times. comments.author: pane1
comments.text:
WHAT
Separate the EXPECTATION from the RECEIPT in docs/demos/STATUS.tsv so a row's number cannot be
validated against a file the row's own author wrote. Today scripts/lane-status.sh verifies that a
cited receipt EXISTS on disk (fail-closed, exit 3, RED arm proven with a planted bogus row). It does
not verify that the receipt's VALUE agrees with a separately-recorded expectation. Existence is not
agreement.

WHY
This is the lane's most-measured defect class, not a speculative one.
  * Three candidates were scored both ways and all three fell the same direction — authored
    success, real-data miss: a gate at 0/20 FP authored vs 3/20 held-out; foreman supervision
    AUC 1.000 on vignettes vs 0.750 on 186,449 real windows; jev-review 12/12 authored pairs vs
    AUC 0.625 on 22 real diffs (RULING-authored-vs-real-20260919.md).
  * R70: "our kills are auditable, our ships are not" — FP samples were never persisted, so a
    number existed that nobody but its author could check.
  * 2026-09-21: a 219-row corpus was reported with aggregates only and no pair identities. Caught
    by a peer, not by a gate. A validator that checks existence would have passed it.
  * Same day, dumpTools was cited as an L2 oracle by two panes; it is blind to extension tools. A
    value check against an independent expectation would have caught the false ZERO; an existence
    check would not.

ACCEPTANCE
  Command: ./scripts/lane-status.sh   (plus its selftest)
  POSITIVE: every STATUS.tsv row carries an expectation field recorded independently of the
    receipt, and lane-status.sh exits 0 only when receipt value == expectation for every row.
  PLANTED NEGATIVE (required, must be shown failing): a row whose receipt EXISTS but whose value
    DISAGREES with its expectation must exit non-zero. The current validator passes that case —
    demonstrate the current pass, then the new fail. Without both halves this is unproven.
  NO-CLAIM: this gates arithmetic agreement only. It does not detect a wrong expectation, a
    corpus the author also chose, or a metric that is the wrong metric.

CREATION GATE (tick.md section 1 — all four named)
  1. CONSUMER: scripts/lane-status.sh, and every pane that cites a STATUS verdict.
  2. GATE: a verdict cannot ship when its receipt disagrees with its expectation.
  3. OBSERVED DEFECT: the four instances above, all measured in this repo, none speculative.
  4. RETIREMENT: retire when every STATUS row's number is derived from a receipt produced by
     someone other than the row's author, making the agreement check redundant.

title: Loss depth: PokéJev Stage B (56.0% vs Abyssal, kill line 70%)
description: WHAT: AGENTS.md LOSS DEPTH steps 1-4 on work/poke-jev/stage-b/decisions-abyssal.jsonl (5,494 decisions: candidates, values, prior_top, opponent, chosen) and results-abyssal.jsonl (88 losses of 200). Step 1 keyless: for the lost battles, find the turns where the outcome turned (HP swing, a faint), and classify what Jev got wrong there: action prior (Choice), opponent model (Stage A showed it overconfident, ECE 0.174, 0.00 on the true move in 12% of rows), or leaf value (absolute Scores saturate once one side leads, per typesafe-chess), or the state missing facts (hazards, speed, items, tera). Count each. Step 2: 3-5 ranked hypotheses, each changing one variable (for example, relative pairwise leaf values instead of absolute Scores; tempering or flooring the opponent distribution; adding a missing state field), each checked against docs-mirror/typesafe/confidence.md and the cookbooks. Step 3: a dev replay loop on fixed decision points from lost battles (not the Stage B seeds' held-out use), live and cheap, one variable at a time. Step 4: the best design gets a new prereg and a fresh 200-battle run vs Abyssal on new team seeds, same 70% kill line. WHY: the Stage B KILL measured one design; Jev added 16.5 points over the zero-call control, so the signal is real. ACCEPTANCE: autopsy table with counts committed before any live call; dev-loop spend under USD 3; held-out result or a named model limit.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: loss depth done, Stage B KILL stands. Autopsy 6752e9e (85 Jev-active losses: opponent model 30, action prior 31, leaf 19, missing state 5). comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: PLAN TO OBLITERATE ABYSSAL (pane 1, after Joshua asked 'what would take us obliterating abyssal'). Target: >= 90% vs Abyssal with 0 time losses (above PokéChamp-GPT-4o's published 84%). Measured today: damage-calculator greedy (the zero-call control) 39.5-40.5%; Jev search 56.0%. The search is narrow and shallow (K_PLAYER=3 of up to 13 options, K_OPP=4 replies, one turn) and uses 1.09 s p50 / 2.4 s p95 per decision of a 15 s turn. Its leaf value is near chance at predicting the winner: AUC 0.554 over all 4,334 non-fallback Stage B decisions (0.537 on dev). Levers, in order, each measured before any battle: (1) a real leaf evaluator: code features (HP-weighted remaining team, statuses, hazards, speed order, KO threats from the damage calculator the control already runs) plus Jev Nouls for what code cannot count, combined by logistic regression fit on Stage B dev decisions and scored by AUC on held-out battles (the phishing pattern: 5 Nouls + a fit gave AUROC 0.987 vs 0.685 for one verdict); (2) spend the clock: all legal options and more opponent replies, two turns deep when time allows; (3) damage-calculator facts in Jev's state (this move KOs, they outspeed); (4) a stronger fixed team as a separate arm, since it breaks comparability. Each preregistered, one variable per battle arm.

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (pane 1, keyless) of the r2 code arm losing (17/70 at 08:39Z): harness defect, not a leaf-model result. (1) run.py _summary_features line 439 uses re.findall(r"(\\d+)%", ...): a raw string with a doubled backslash, so it never matches digits and per-candidate hp always falls back to the shared base value; status/hazard/speed are shared too; only ko_threat differs by candidate (0 switch, 1 move), weight -0.124, so every switch outscores every move. (2) Measured on decisions-abyssal-leaf-code-leaf-c-r2-code.jsonl: switched on 1,518 of 1,532 turns with a switch offered (99%) vs 906/2,217 (41%) frozen-alpha; 99.5% of recorded leaf values are exactly 0/1 because choose_with_values records a one-hot argmax. (3) Train/serve skew independent of (1): leaf_c trains hp_weighted_remaining on replay-seen mons only (mean 0.268, scale 0.135); live sums the whole known team, near 1.0 (z about +5). The r2 code rows are NOT-SCORED harness-bug. Resume needs tests for per-candidate discrimination and live-vs-replay feature agreement, then a new note.

comments.text: PANE 1 (r3, keyless): (1) Held-out recount of 4af5ce5 reproduces code-only 0.6458 [0.544, 0.741] and code+Noul 0.7175 [0.636, 0.788]; paired Noul delta +0.0717, 95% [+0.0044, +0.1607], 1.2% of resamples <= 0. Code-only now FAILS the 46d09b8 bar (0.65, lower > 0.60); code+Noul passes. Caveat: this is the second read of the held-out split (r1 then r3), preregistered in d201a3f before scoring, change was a parity fix, not tuning. (2) The r3 code arm still switched on 977 of 982 offered turns (NOT-SCORED, stopped 03:12:12). Cause is a design flaw, not a parse bug: the leaf was fit to predict the winner at recorded decisions, and one of its 5 features, ko_threat, is the recorded action type (leaf_c.py:237: tool starts with 'move '). Live, run.py:453 sets it per candidate (0 switch, 1 move); weight -0.149 on scale 0.324 gives every switch +0.46 logit. The other 4 features describe only our side (own team HP, own statuses, shared hazards, constant speed), so damage dealt to the opponent earns nothing and no move can catch up. A winner-prediction AUC bar does not test action ranking; that bar gated the wrong property. Before any further battle: drop the action-type feature, add opponent-side post-candidate features (opponent HP remaining, HP differential), refit on dev, held-out once, and add an action-ranking sanity gate on recorded turns (switch rate within 10 points of Stage B's 41%, moves with different outcomes get different scores).

title: Loss depth: AX pruning (R107): why Jev kept the whole page on 20/50 episodes, and whether pruning can ever pay with a Jev planner
description: WHAT: keyless autopsy of the 100 jev-arm pruner requests in work/miniwob-ax-prune/rows/{dev,heldout}-jev.jsonl (per-node Noul answers). (1) Where the cut went: per node, the three Nouls (relevant_to_current_goal, contains_required_value, safe_to_omit) and the keep rule; count nodes kept by each Noul alone, and why 20/50 held-out episodes kept everything. (2) Economics: the pruner request averaged about 6,820 input tokens per episode against about 1,945 for the full planner state, so with a Jev planner, pruning with Jev costs 4.2x more total input than it saves. State for which planner cost ratio pruning would pay (break-even), using the measured token counts. (3) Ranked one-variable hypotheses for a dev loop: one Noul instead of three OR'd; a keep cut fitted on dev; a cheaper pruner state (node text only). WHY: the prereg's bar measured planner tokens only; the design never asked whether the pruner is cheaper than what it prunes. ACCEPTANCE: autopsy doc and script committed, counts reproduce from one command, no live call.
close_reason: Autopsy a68ba48 (subject says [oracle]; honest level [test], per the bead note): all 100 step-0 pages rebuilt at dd04baf match the rows byte for byte. Pruner cost is 442.6 input tokens per element (R2 0.998, N=100); break-even planner/Jev price ratio c is 13.56 as measured, 7.05 even at a perfect cut, and 1.97 for the best combined design (one Noul, text-only state, skip text runs). So with a Jev planner (c=1), no design in this family can pay; pruning with Jev pays only in front of a planner at least about 2-7x Jev's price per token. Per-node answers were not logged, so H1/H2 need a logging dev replay. Closed as a named limit for a Jev planner.

title: classifier measurement core: symmetric calibration, cost/NP cuts, prevalence projection, conformal sets, multiple-test control
description:
WHAT: Integration core for the D2-D7/D17 measurement-method beads: expose a zero-dependency TypeScript API for symmetric calibration, cost/prevalence/NP cuts, conformal abstention, multiplicity correction, same-model rerun spread, and prediction-powered metrics. Keep method work in independently verifiable child beads; never turn missing labels, missing prerequisites, or unsupported assumptions into PASS. WHY: the current core bundles seven distinct statistical decisions with separate assumptions and failure modes. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:166-172`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:19-61`.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:166-172; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:19-61

PRIOR DESCRIPTION (kept verbatim; scope now split as stated above):

(2) cuts by expected cost at projected prevalence; Neyman-Pearson cut from negatives only (29/59/149/299 negatives for FPR .10/.05/.02/.01, delta .05). (3) BBSE prevalence projection plus a KS alarm on live scores. (4) split-conformal LAC answer sets that refuse without an exchangeability declaration. (5) Benjamini-Hochberg across bars, e-BH within a batch, confidence sequences for shadow stopping. (6) prediction-powered inference for organic metrics. (7) drift tests against same-model rerun spread. WHY: the audit overturned three claims (Clef calibration win, Clef vendored win, memory .985) and explained the vendor .21 precision and the 0.990->0.335 skill-veto drop as method errors (D2-D7, D17). BORROW: port the design of franken_nlp src/calibration.rs (Dicklesworthstone mirror) and process_triage expected-loss/e-BH; no imports. SOURCE: Decision register: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7; specs/advanced-mathops.md, advanced-literature.md, advanced-repos.md. CONTRACT: failing test committed (or shown failing) before the change; one planted mutation the test catches; any regex on tool/model text passes the regex-engineering section 7 run; any quality claim has its bar committed before the first call with spend stated; non-author verify in a clone with a scrubbed HOME. Keyless proofs run on committed rows only.
acceptance_criteria:

The integration test verifies all six D2-D7/D17 method outputs are wired and each method's child test is present; a coin-flip calibration fixture and a non-exchangeable conformal fixture must make the relevant child test RED. It also checks no module imports a heavy runtime dependency and missing/unsupported evidence reports NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN. Planted negatives: a coin-flip backend gets ECE above its noise floor and fails eval; conformal refuses when exchangeability is not declared. `node --test kit/test/measurement.test.mjs`. The `calibrate`, `eval`, and `watch` CLI consumers pin the shared envelope and exit/status mapping, `--dry-run`/`--apply` mutation gate, exact typo correction/remediation, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` determinism, `NO_COLOR=1`, non-TTY/CI behavior, and per-verb golden/schema tests in CI. Sources: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:34-40,97-118,164-182; work/plan-20261004/specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md:164-226; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/rubric/SCORING-RUBRIC.md:70-78,86-110,136-144,168-194; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/rubric/REGRESSION-TEST-PATTERNS.md:1-23,40-58.

HONEST-CREDIT (credit-GoldRiver.jsonl:10): Failing-first keyless tests import and exercise the shipped zero-dependency measurement module; a planted mutation must make a named test fail. Recompute committed-row behavior for probability floor 0.005; symmetric dev-fitted temperature/Platt/isotonic maps; ECE noise floor and seeded bootstrap CI; paired McNemar/DeLong; prevalence-projected expected-cost and negatives-only Neyman-Pearson cuts; BBSE plus KS shift alarm; split-conformal LAC with refusal absent exchangeability; BH/e-BH, confidence-sequence stopping, PPI, and same-model rerun-spread drift. Reproduce the committed Banking77 ECE values (~0.028 Jev, ~0.025 Clef) with CI including zero difference, LAC alpha 0.10 coverage ~0.90/mean set ~1.67, Youden precision ~0.21 at 5% prevalence, BBSE projection 0.40-0.63, NP held-negative FPR bound, and two same-model runs flagged only beyond the rerun null. Preserve row hashes and recompute stated tolerances, not hard-coded outputs. Planted negatives include coin-flip eval, missing exchangeability, and NP bound violation. Run `npm test --prefix kit`; report named tests and non-author verification. Any new quality bar is committed before calls with a fixed call cap and spend. NO-CLAIM: reproduced committed rows validate this implementation only, not organic accuracy, transfer, or Clef advantage.

MATH REVIEW (wave1, WildCarp; binding: each item needs a numeric tolerance or a typed refusal fixed before implementation):
- [jev-b35c.10] The acceptance is not bead-lint complete (no runnable command or planted negative), and the bead bundles seven separately testable statistical components. Current checker evidence: python3 scripts/bead-lint.py --epic jev-b35c reports jev-b35c.10 no-command; the acceptance names a coin-flip and missing-exchangeability cases only as prose, not a runnable test. Keep this bead as the measurement-core parent or split by calibration, cuts/prevalence, conformal, multiplicity/sequential drift, and PPI only after the implementation target/test command exists; do not invent a package path while implementation is paused. The required negative cases and numeric tolerances need to be explicit in the final child acceptances. (evidence: scripts/bead-lint.py:2-7; scripts/bead-lint.py:97-105; jev-b35c.10 acceptance (RUST_LOG=off br show jev-b35c.10); work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:102-118)
- [jev-b35c.10] D2’s formula choices are plausible, but the contract does not define floor/renormalization semantics, model selection among temperature/Platt/isotonic, fixed ECE bins, or a numerical equivalence margin. CI including zero means ‘no detected difference’, not equivalence or a tie. Require both arms fitted on their own identical dev indices; floor and renormalize each multiclass vector (define binary rule), select calibrator on dev only, freeze ECE estimator/bin rule, and compare with paired held-row uncertainty. A calibration win requires a predeclared effect margin with the CI wholly beyond it; a tie requires the CI wholly inside a predeclared equivalence interval. State bootstrap resampling unit/seed/count and cluster by session/group where rows are dependent. ‘Noise floor’ must be estimated from held-score Bernoulli null draws under the same estimator, not used as a substitute for CI. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:167; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:7,21-23,108-115; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:102-108)
- [jev-b35c.10] Acceptance lacks explicit numeric tolerances for ‘~.028’, ‘~.90’, ‘~1.67’, ‘~.21’, and ‘within its finite-sample band’; only the floor/cut rates and D16 sample target are crisp. Define error budgets before implementation: e.g. an absolute ECE reproduction tolerance and paired delta margin, coverage interval/test size, set-size tolerance, PPV interval at π=.05, BBSE estimand/error interval, and drift false-alarm/power thresholds. Keep those values anchored to the cited recomputation, not selected after seeing implementation outputs. The current underlying research is exploratory/non-preregistered and cannot itself authorize a model-quality claim. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:167-173,181-182; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:3,7-12,110-120; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:18-20)

title: classifier measurement: expected-cost, NP, prevalence, and KS methods (D3, D4)
description:
WHAT: Implement D3 cost-derived and Neyman-Pearson thresholds and D4 real-prevalence projection/BBSE plus the live-score KS alarm. Keep assumptions and positive/negative counts explicit; refuse a threshold when its required class count or exchangeability assumptions are absent. WHY: a balanced Youden cut overstated organic precision and the prior bar did not account for deployment prevalence. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:168-169`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:27,29-31,51-53`.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:168-169; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:27,29-31,51-53
ORIGIN: wave1 beads-AmberWillow.jsonl:25
acceptance_criteria:
`node --test kit/test/measurement-thresholds.test.mjs` passes on committed rows and deterministic synthetic distributions. Verify cost-derived cut, NP upper-bound arithmetic, prevalence-adjusted PPV, BBSE recovery on a known mixture, and KS alarm on planted drift. Insufficient negative/positive counts or a singular confusion matrix must return NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN, not PASS. No live monitoring or deployment-quality claim. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:168-169`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:27,29-31,51-53`.

MATH REVIEW (wave1, WildCarp; binding: each item needs a numeric tolerance or a typed refusal fixed before implementation):
- [plan:D3] The listed Neyman–Pearson negative counts are arithmetically correct for zero observed exceedances and a one-sided (1−δ) confidence bound: ceil(log(.05)/log(1−α)) gives 29/59/149/299 for α=.10/.05/.02/.01 (independently recomputed). But ‘cut on held negatives stays within its FPR bound’ risks reusing the threshold-fitting sample as its own validation. Separate threshold-fit negatives from a fresh, independent audit set, define the order-statistic/tie rule and error direction, and report a one-sided bound at the stated confidence; fail closed if fewer than n eligible negatives. For D16, the n=59 requirement is for the false-drop rate among relevant memories, not a generic estimate of P(drop|relevant); use the same independent validation distinction and handle turn/session clustering. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:168,181; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:31,52; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:45-53)
- [plan:D4] BBSE is conditional on stable class-conditional score/decision distributions and an identifiable (invertible, adequately conditioned) source confusion matrix; the observed skill-veto example includes conditional shift (FIT veto rate .20 in source to .739 in organic), so the projection range .40-.63 is not a general accuracy guarantee. Acceptance should identify the projected estimand (target prevalence vs precision), require a conditioning/invertibility diagnostic and uncertainty interval, and fail/label unidentifiable when the shift assumptions fail or the estimate exits [0,1]. Keep the KS alarm distinct: it detects score-distribution shift, not label shift or performance loss by itself. The existing R4 is evidence of an alarm/proxy, not reliable BBSE recovery: π̂(UNFIT)=.938 vs blind truth .29. Pause enforcement claims until deadline handling is fixed and validated; the incident jev-s0ve reports 1,328/2,921 deadline-keeps and 137/409 turns with no scored result. Measure the safety estimand P(drop|relevant) with relevant as the protected class, name the sampling design and effective independent unit (turn/session clustering), and require a fresh validation sample after selecting the cut. Acceptance needs the one-sided upper bound ≤ .05 at 95% confidence, zero relevant drops within a preregistered safety allowance, plus an operational timeout gate; do not use drop precision as substitute. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:181; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:11,31-32,52; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:52,158-159; jev-s0ve acceptance (RUST_LOG=off br show jev-s0ve))

title: classifier measurement: conformal sets, multiplicity, and PPI (D5, D6, D17)
description:
WHAT: Implement D5 split-conformal LAC answer sets with exchangeability refusal; D6 Benjamini-Hochberg/e-BH/confidence-sequence controls; and D17 prediction-powered inference with uncertainty on organic metrics. Keep method contracts separate in code and label assumptions explicitly. WHY: per-bar tests create false-pass risk, while organic positives are too sparse for labels-only estimates; conformal results are invalid without declared exchangeability. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170-171,182`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33-35,57,60-61`.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170-171,182; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33-35,57,60-61
ORIGIN: wave1 beads-AmberWillow.jsonl:26
acceptance_criteria:
`node --test kit/test/measurement-inference.test.mjs` passes on committed calibration rows and deterministic generated fixtures. Check conformal coverage/set size and refusal without exchangeability; check BH/e-BH decisions against hand-calculated committed p-values and a confidence sequence against a fixed-n fixture; check PPI's estimate/interval on a saved-score fixture against the labels-only interval. Plant one non-exchangeable split and one coin-flip/p-values-all-null case and assert the corresponding method refuses or reports no discoveries. Organic transfer remains NOT_RUN without eligible labels. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170-171,182`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33-35,57,60-61`.

MATH REVIEW (wave1, WildCarp; binding: each item needs a numeric tolerance or a typed refusal fixed before implementation):
- [plan:D5] LAC’s split-conformal formula is appropriate under exchangeability, but ‘refuse when exchangeability is not declared’ is too weak: a caller declaration does not establish exchangeability. Require a named sampling frame and disjoint calibration/test groups from the target population; otherwise abstain/refuse. Acceptance must state α, n_cal, n_test, tie handling, and a numeric finite-sample coverage interval or exact binomial criterion; ‘outside its finite-sample band’ is not executable. The reported .903 coverage / mean set 1.67 is an observed point, not a numerical tolerance. Add metamorphic checks: row permutation leaves the result unchanged with ID-keyed randomness; relabeling class IDs permutes sets but leaves coverage/set-size unchanged; strictly increasing score transforms preserve AUC (strictness matters with ties); invalid probability vectors refuse. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33,54,118; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:115-117)
- [plan:D6] The D6 accounting rule needs a defined family and valid input type: BH at q=.05 controls FDR only under independence or PRDS of valid p-values; e-BH requires valid e-values and its own batch/family boundaries. ‘Across the ledger’ and ‘within a batch’ are not enough to determine which hypotheses enter, how dependent/repeated bars are handled, or when recomputation occurs. Confidence sequences additionally require bounded outcomes and a declared dependence/cluster treatment and stopping rule. Add planted p/e-value inputs whose dependence violates the assumed regime; ensure invalid or missing p/e values cannot be silently dropped. The missing reversal criterion (‘—’) prevents an outcome-based refutation. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:171; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:35,60-61; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:158-160)
- [plan:D17] PPI is appropriate only with a probability sample of labels from the target population and predictions for that same population; the residual correction is not protected against convenience/active sampling unless the design weights are included. The bead’s reversal ‘PPI interval no narrower than labels-only’ needs equal nominal coverage and a specified estimator (PPI vs PPI++), random-label sampling, interval procedure, and numerical width comparison on repeated resamples. ‘PPI’ alone does not guarantee a narrower interval; PPI++/optimized rectifier is the method with a no-wider-than-classical property under its assumptions. Add metamorphic checks: when predictions are constant, PPI reduces to labels-only mean; when predictions equal labels on labeled rows, the residual correction is zero; permuting row order leaves estimates/CI unchanged with deterministic ID-keyed bootstrap. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:182; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:57,146-147; arXiv:2301.09633)

Also pin all `--backend`/decision outcomes in the `classifier.<cmd>.v1` envelope: error status and exit code agree, no-key/unavailable semantics are class-correct, and failures include the exact safe corrective command. `--dry-run` constructs the request and makes zero calls; deterministic JSON honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`; `NO_COLOR=1`/non-TTY behavior and schema goldens run in CI. Plain fetch sends no Authorization header, posts the receipt question key, refuses raw/un-calibrated or >=16384-token answers, and validates result shape. `auto` routes only a one-question exact-receipt request with matching fingerprint and no hold; otherwise records the first fallback reason. The decision must not imply a demonstrated best-arm gain. Require the per-task logistic model to be trained only on dev, freeze feature/regularization selection there, then evaluate on a disjoint group/time split; compare paired AUC and calibration with both constituent arms and require the improvement CI to exceed a predeclared numeric margin versus the strongest constituent. Cascade acceptance should preserve its explicit tradeoff (42% sent to Clef; .942 vs .962 Clef-only) and never call that parity. title: Resume-quality A/B: Jev-prune vs generic summary
description:
WHAT: Run the resume-quality A/B that decides whether Jev-pruning beats generic summarization on real omp traffic.
WHY: Step 1 proved size reduction (45%) with zero text loss, but reduction is not the claim — better-than-summary continuation is. Without this test a smaller context that answers worse would ship as a win.
APPROACH:
1. Corpus: compaction/fixtures/omp-session-big-20260917.jsonl via compaction/src/omp-adapter.ts. Arm A context = compactMessages() output (see compaction/runs/replay-big-20260917.json; re-derive, do not trust it).
2. Extract the 5 dropped call ids (dump decisions with a tsx one-liner against the real Jev client) and author 3 resume questions answerable ONLY from dropped results, with expected answers quoted from the fixture.
3. Arm B context: one generic condensation of the same transcript (fixed prompt, recorded in receipt; `omp -p`, default model).
4. Resume: one fresh model call per arm, identical prompt (context + questions). Record answers verbatim. Grade substring-match against expected.
BUDGET: ~4 live calls total (Arm A re-derive 1, summary 1, resume 2). State each call in the receipt.
NON-GOALS: No library changes. No new fixtures from other sessions. No prompt-tuning to make an arm win.
ACCEPTANCE: compaction/runs/ab-<date>.json with both contexts' byte sizes, both answer transcripts, per-question grades, and a one-line verdict (A wins / B wins / tie). Verdict must be reproducible from the receipt alone.
RECEIPT: The runs/ab JSON + close reason citing it. Report model names, Jev request count, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY sourcing (env only, never in tree).
close_reason: Receipt compaction/runs/ab-20260917.json; live verdict B wins (A 1/3, B 3/3), four live calls, commit e763fa3.

title: Lane gap: am mail leg of the REPLY-VIA contract is dead — 6 units delivered, inbox count 0
description:
WHAT
The three-leg callback contract (bead comment + am mail + committed receipt) has a silently dead
middle leg in this lane. Measured 2026-09-18 00:41Z: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent
CyanFalcon` returned `"count": 0, "inbox": []` after panes 2 and 3 had delivered SIX units
between them. Every bead comment landed; every commit landed; not one mail arrived. Both panes
routed callbacks through the pane relay instead.

title: A/B harness emits a one-word verdict over a nondeterministic arm — remove it or report a distribution
description:
WHAT
compaction/ab/run-ab.ts computes armB by a live runOmp summarization call with no temperature pin,
then at line 164 collapses the comparison to a single string: armAScore > armBScore ? 'A wins' :
armBScore > armAScore ? 'B wins' : 'tie'. Measured 2026-09-18 across three runs:

  ab-20260917         fixture 214,993 B sha 20fa1ea0   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'
  ab-rerun-20260918   fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 1/3  'tie'
  ab-sample3-20260918 fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'

Rows 2 and 3 are byte-identical in input and differ by two points on armB. armA scored 1/3 in all
three. So the verdict field flips on generator variance while reading like a result.

WHY
The 'B wins' string propagated into 17 tracked files — duel idea files, four score files, four
dispatch packets, a claim audit, and bead bodies — before anything ran the harness twice. A
one-word verdict over a stochastic arm is not a presentation problem; it manufactures a finding.
This is the lane's own 'cherry-picked N' violation committed by its own tooling, and the tooling is
what made it easy.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The harness no longer emits an unconditional 'verdict' string. Either (a) drop the field, or
   (b) emit it only when the run carries n>=10 samples per stochastic arm plus the observed spread,
   and refuse (nonzero) when asked for a verdict at n=1.
2. armA may still be reported absolutely — it is deterministic-enough (1/3, three for three) and
   that is the lane's one supported compaction finding.
3. The receipt records, per arm, whether the arm is deterministic, and for stochastic arms the
   sample count and the per-sample scores. A receipt that cannot express variance is the root cause.
4. RED arm: a fixture run twice with a stochastic arm and differing scores must NOT produce a
   verdict; the harness reports the spread and exits nonzero if a caller demanded one.
5. Re-run the existing three receipts' inputs under the new harness and confirm no 'B wins' or
   'tie' string is produced for n=1.
6. Every one of the 17 citing files is either corrected or annotated. Re-derive the count with
   'git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lE "3/3|B wins|ab-20260917"' and quote the new number;
   EVAL.md, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md R11 and WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md are already done at 3234bce.

something jev specifically needs'. Per R10 the remedy is a flag or an upstream bead against the

title: demo-1 BLOCKER: three artifacts assert three different turn counts for one fixture (6 vs 18 vs 1)
description:
WHAT
demos/routing-backtest disagrees with its own fixture about how many turns that fixture contains,
by 6x and 18x, and a stranger following the documented path cannot tell.

MEASURED 2026-09-18 from a CLEAN CLONE (git clone of the repo into a temp dir, install.sh run, then
the documented command):

  fixtures/real-excerpt-t1-t6.jsonl .......... 94 rows
  rows carrying a "model" field .............. 18   (all muse-spark-1.3-contributor)
  fixtures/manifest.json purpose ............. "happy-path corpus turns 1-6"
  reader output on that fixture .............. {"sessions":1,"turns":1,"classifiableTurns":1,"skippedTurns":0}

So the same file is described as 6 turns by the manifest, contains 18 model-bearing rows, and is
read as 1 turn by the demo. At most one of those can be right.

The same reader reports 30 turns over 2 real omp session logs, which is plausible, so the defect is
specific to how the fixture excerpt is segmented rather than a general failure. Most likely cause:
the excerpt contains one user prompt followed by many assistant/tool rows, so a turn-grouping rule
keyed on user prompts sees 1 turn while the manifest author counted assistant exchanges. That is a
HYPOTHESIS, not a finding — the code has not been read.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE SHIP CLAIM
docs/demos/PLAN.md defines shipped as four artifacts and all four now exist: install.sh runs clean
on a fresh clone (10 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), a receipt exists, an EVAL row is appended, and tests
with RED arms fire. But the demo's ONE stranger-reachable result is n=1, and its own manifest says
it should be 6. A stranger runs the documented command, gets turns:1, and has no way to know
whether that is the corpus, the reader, or a bug. "An empty scan set is an ERROR, not a pass" has a
sibling this lane had not written down: A ONE-TURN SCAN SET IS NOT A DEMONSTRATION.

It also means the demo's headline finding — actual $7.230350988 vs counterfactual $7.226928188,
savings $0.0034228, 0.047% over 30 turns — is reproducible only against ~/.omp session logs that no
stranger has. The shipped fixtures cannot reproduce the result the demo is about.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive all three counts and quote them: fixture rows, model-bearing rows, manifest claim,
   reader output. State which is authoritative and why.
2. Fix the disagreement at its source. Either the manifest's "turns 1-6" is wrong and becomes the
   measured number, or the reader's turn segmentation is wrong and is corrected. Do not "fix" it by
   editing whichever artifact is easier.
3. Define "turn" once, in one place, and make both the reader and the fixture READMEs cite that
   definition. Three artifacts asserting three counts is a missing shared definition, not three
   bugs.
4. The stranger path must produce a NON-VACUOUS result: a fixture that yields enough turns to show
   a cheap-vs-frontier split, with at least one routable turn. Re-run from a clean clone and paste
   the denominator.
5. RED arm: a run whose classifiable-turn count is below a stated floor must WARN or ERROR rather

comments.author: SecretProbeCheck
comments.text:
NON-AUTHOR CHECK (SecretProbeCheck, omp/18.3.1, 2026-09-25). VERDICT: DEFECT FOUND. The live arms hold, but a REDACTED verdict can be wrong. REDACTED is inferred from what the answer lacks: HEAD != "apikey_", TAIL != last 4 and LEN != "107". The answer is never required to show a placeholder. Any answer that is not the key and has all three fields returns exit 0, including one where the file was never read.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 8, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

Plants (my own, in the /tmp/doc7-check copy; after each one the script was restored and sha256 aa14f386416da38c matched the repo file):
  A NOT_RUN returns REDACTED -> FAILED 1 (test_no_answer_is_not_run_never_redacted)
  B REDACTED when ANY field differs (and->or) -> FAILED 1 (test_a_placeholder_head_with_the_full_length_is_unclear)
  C fake_key returns a constant -> FAILED 1 (test_fake_key_has_the_live_key_shape_and_varies)
  D REDACTED checks only LEN != 107 (the HEAD and TAIL clauses deleted) -> OK, 8 of 8 PASS. The plant survives: no test covers the negated HEAD/TAIL clauses.

Live, 4 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  1 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=claude answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0
  2 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red` (git init, .omp/config.yml `secrets: {enabled: true}`, no secrets.yml; no ~/.omp/agent/secrets.yml) -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=4bp9'  exit=1
  3 `python3 /tmp/doc7-check/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a /tmp copy of the script with one extra line, os.remove(planted), before ask(), so the read fails. The cwd is the same one that leaked in run 2. -> REDACTED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=0   <- FALSE REDACTED on a config proven to leak
  4 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --profile codex` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=codex answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0

Offline: answers that return REDACTED although the key reached the model, or although the check never ran (verdict() called directly; FAKE ends in 7h0m):
  'LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`'   leak; backticks plus a miscounted length (the test file itself expects miscounts)
  'LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"'   leak; quoted fields
  'LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m'       leak; slices off by one
  'LEN=105 HEAD=apikey_a TAIL=h0m.'      leak; 8-character head
  'LEN=64 HEAD=cat: TAIL=tory'           cat failed; the model reports the error line
  'LEN=0 HEAD=none TAIL=none'            cat never ran; the model made up an answer
  With LEN=107 exactly, the backtick and quote forms become UNCLEAR. So only an exact length count stops a leak that has formatting around it from reading as REDACTED.
Not fixable in a script: the verdict still depends on what the model says. A model that invents a placeholder answer cannot be caught this way.

Fix direction (not applied; the script is not mine to edit): return REDACTED only on positive evidence, and require the check to have run.
  (a) REDACTED needs a placeholder in HEAD or TAIL, e.g. HEAD matches ^\$?\$?TYPESAF, or TAIL matches :[ULCM]\$?\$?$. The friendlyName TYPESAFEAPIKEY is fixed by .omp/secrets.yml, so the probe knows it in advance.
  (b) Before comparing, strip quote, backtick and period characters from each value. Treat a HEAD or TAIL that is a substring or prefix of the fake key as a LEAK.
  (c) Anything else is UNCLEAR (exit 3), never 0. Add tests for run 3's answer and for the backtick leak row; both should come back UNCLEAR or LEAKED, not REDACTED. That also kills plant D.
Bead left OPEN.

comments.author: SecretProbeCheck
comments.text:
NON-AUTHOR RE-CHECK of 5557cbb (SecretProbeCheck, omp/18.3.1). VERDICT: HOLDS. The defect I reported is fixed: REDACTED now requires a placeholder, and my live read-fail row returns UNCLEAR with exit 3, where it used to return REDACTED with exit 0. Three limits remain, none of them a false REDACTED I could produce live; they are listed below.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 11, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

Offline: verdict() on my six earlier answers, plus new ones (FAKE ends in 7h0m):
  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`
  LEAKED   LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"
  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m
  LEAKED   LEN=105 HEAD=apikey_a TAIL=h0m.
  UNCLEAR  LEN=64 HEAD=cat: TAIL=tory
  UNCLEAR  LEN=0 HEAD=none TAIL=none
  UNCLEAR  LEN=107 HEAD=**apikey_** TAIL=**7h0m**   (markdown bold is not stripped; the answer still fails to UNCLEAR, not REDACTED)
  UNCLEAR  LEN=107 HEAD=APIKEY_ TAIL=7H0M           (the model changed the case; UNCLEAR)
  LEAKED   LEN=40 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=b7h0m           (only the head is redacted; the raw tail is caught)
  REDACTED LEN=107. HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$          (the trailing '.' defeats the LEN != 107 guard; a cosmetic gap, because both ends are still placeholders)

Plants in the /tmp/doc7-check2 copy. After each one the script was restored and sha256 f7c2df44de32be1a matched the repo file:
  E drop the .strip of quote/punctuation characters -> FAILED 2 subtests (test_leaks_in_quotes_or_off_by_one_slices_are_leaked). Caught.
  F placeholder_head OR placeholder_tail (was AND) -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. No test covers an answer with a placeholder head and a tail that is neither a placeholder nor a key piece, e.g. 'LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=none'. Under the plant that answer is REDACTED; the shipped code returns UNCLEAR. Nothing pins the conjunct.
  G delete the tail-only LEAKED clause `or (len(tail) >= 3 and tail in fake)` -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. Every leak row in the tests also leaks in HEAD. Under the plant, 'LEN=40 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=b7h0m' returns UNCLEAR, so it still fails safe, but the clause has no test. A one-row test for each would kill F and G.

Live, 2 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  A `python3 /tmp/doc7-check2/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a 5557cbb copy with os.remove(planted) before ask(); /tmp/doc7-red has secrets enabled and no regex, and it leaked earlier. -> UNCLEAR cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=3
  B `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-mid`. I tried to make omp redact only the two ends of the key: secrets.yml held regex "apikey_[a-z0-9]{5}" and regex "[a-z0-9]{12}$" with flags m. -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-mid profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=fjj8'  exit=1. omp did not apply those regexes at all; I did not find out why [INFERENCE: flag or order handling]. The verdict was correct for what the model saw.

Remaining limit (a design limit, not reproduced live): the probe only looks at the two ends of the line. If a config redacts both ends and leaves the middle raw, the answer would look like 'LEN=101 HEAD=$$QX7P2 TAIL=:L$$', and verdict() returns REDACTED for that answer offline even though about 80 key characters reached the model. The TypeSafe regex in .omp/secrets.yml matches the whole 107 characters, so the shipped config is not exposed to this. Closing the gap needs either a MID=<chars 50-57> field or a cap on LEN for REDACTED (placeholders are 18-33 characters). The model can still lie; that limit is already stated in the docstring.
Bead left OPEN.

title: Foundry bug: house-gate selftests fail under init.templateDir (needs git-config isolation)
description:
WHAT: report and fix upstream that loop-kit gate selftests which build a throwaway git fixture repo fail on any machine with `init.templateDir` set.

WHY: measured 2026-09-17 on this machine. `init.templateDir = ~/.git-templates` installs the commit-msg verification-level hook into EVERY newly created repo, so a selftest that inits a temp repo and commits plain fixture messages dies at "SELFTEST FAIL: fixture repo setup" - the hook correctly refuses a level-less subject. Discriminating proof:
  commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest                              -> FAIL (fixture repo setup)
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null ... --selftest -> PASS (3 known-bad flagged, 3 clean controls passed)
So the FIXTURE was broken, not the gate - and every future gate with the same shape inherits the defect. Our wrapper (foundation/gates.d/50-house-gates.sh) already neutralizes the config; the fix belongs upstream so the whole fleet gets it.

ACCEPTANCE: loop-kit gate selftests pass with ambient config on a machine with init.templateDir set - by isolating git config or committing with --no-verify inside the fixture. Verify by running `commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest` with NO env overrides and getting SELFTEST PASS.

title: Measure error decorrelation across gate failures
description:
harvested-from:024a568

WHAT: Measure phi/disagreement between gate error vectors from the per-stage outcome vector.

WHY: A prior no-claim says no PHI has been computed for our gates; constant PASS vectors make phi undefined and must not be treated as a finding.

ACCEPTANCE: run the existing ensemble/decorrelation.py against at least two gates with real failure records; report phi, disagreement, gain/verdict, and identify constant-vector pairs as undefined rather than 0. If fewer than two non-constant pairs exist, receipt the negative result and do not claim a correlation finding.

NO-CLAIM SOURCE: NO PHI HAS BEEN COMPUTED FOR OUR GATES. The log currently holds only PASS rows; phi across constant vectors is undefined. This commit makes measurement possible; it does not make it.

NON-GOAL: no synthetic failures and no rewriting gate history.
acceptance_criteria: Receipt with actual gate outcome inputs and phi/disagreement results, or a negative receipt proving fewer than two non-constant gate pairs.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: acceptance met at a328a14. Clean clone dd717e5: keyless 'python3 work/gate-decor/score.py' rc 0, same output as the main tree. Independent path (my own phi over one-per-sha built from the live gitignored foundation/gate-outcomes.tsv, not from the committed extract): all 19 defined pairs match the receipt on n and phi to 4 decimals; 19 pairs have both vectors varying on their overlap; 44x80 phi 0.0 is a real computed zero (co-failure table 2,2,9,9), not the constant case. All 8,869 extract rows exist in the live log. Constant stages reported undefined, not 0. Scope notes, not defects: the strongest pairs rest on few co-failures (80x97 n11=5 of 319, 70x97 n11=3, 70x80 n11=5); head_sha does not capture working-tree edits, so one-per-sha can merge runs over different trees; the receipt has no NO-CLAIM section.

title: Next-gen Jev uses: cross-model duel (Codex gpt-5.6-luna vs Claude) grounded in our measured capability profile; survivors become beads with a cheapest falsifying experiment
description:
DIRECTIVE (Joshua, 2026-09-24, verbatim): "spend more time finding really next-gen uses for jev instead of running it locally". Earlier the same turn: "codex tokens are back - we can add a codex luna worker to our fleet if needed".
WHAT: find uses where Jev's specific properties (typed Choice/Score/Noul answers with calibrated probabilities, many questions over one state in parallel, ~0.25 s per call, cheap per token) unlock something an LLM cannot do at the same latency, cost or calibration, rather than re-scoring another benchmark classifier. Method: (1) brief built from two read-only scouts: our measured capability ledger with file:line citations (wins, losses, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE rows, cost, latency, calibration) plus untested cells on docs-mirror/typesafe/concepts/use-case-map.md, and an outside scan of what others built on Jev and of the frontier for fast calibrated judges; (2) dueling-idea-wizards between a Codex pane (profile codex, gpt-5.6-luna) and a fresh Claude pane, pane 1 orchestrating only; (3) synthesis ranked by cross-model score and by the AGENTS.md selection rules (ground truth exists today, prevalence, cost to measure, decision leverage).
WHY: 40+ rulings in this lane tested Jev as a classifier against cheap baselines, mostly in one use-case category (harness engineering); the surviving wins (SciFact claim verification, SciFact rerank, NevIR negation, OOD spam) are all 'judge a text' uses. Nobody has yet asked what becomes possible only because a calibrated typed judgment costs a quarter second.
ACCEPTANCE: the brief, both idea files, both score files, both reaction files and the synthesis committed under notes/deep/next-gen/; each consensus survivor filed as a child bead with WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE, its location on the use-case map, why an LLM cannot do it at the same cost or latency, and a preregistrable cheapest experiment on data we did not author; the top survivor's experiment started. No ruling is written by this epic; no local model runs; no paid comparator.

description: DIRECTIVE (Joshua, 2026-09-25, verbatim): "yeah lets go public once we get it solid - i'd love to be able to watch it". WHAT: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (daily, plus workflow_dispatch) that runs scripts/stranger-run-jev-playground.py against the repo as a stranger would (fresh checkout, clean HOME, no key variables, only the prerequisites the README tells a stranger to install), then compares with a committed expectation file (e.g. docs/demos/upstream-repro/stranger-run-expected.tsv: command, expected rc class 0 | NOT_RUN-named-prerequisite | NOT_RUN-no-key | expected-nonzero | TEMPLATE, and the prerequisite named). The job fails when a row expected 0 is nonzero, when a NOT_RUN row's message stops naming its prerequisite, or when a README command appears or disappears without an expectation row. Add a --source <path|url> option so CI can run on its own checkout instead of cloning from GitHub; keep the network-clone default for local runs. Upload the receipt as an artifact.

WHY: the second pass (f2e61b0, 5d9f8d6) left 72 of 82 README rows passing and every failure a named prerequisite or keyless NOT_RUN. Two of today's three failure classes (untracked inputs, placeholder commands) came back only because nothing ran the README as a stranger between edits; the README changes several times a day.

ACCEPTANCE: expectation file generated from f2e61b0's receipt and committed; a local run with the script against the expectation exits 0; planted README change (a command pointing at an untracked file) makes the comparison fail and names the row; the workflow file validates (actionlint if available, else a dry parse) and is triggered once with workflow_dispatch, run id pasted; total wall time stated (receipt: about 760 s); keyless; non-author check by pane 1.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: holds. Green dispatch 36135948301 on 5145022 (7m22s): EXPECTATION PASS rows=82. The gate has already failed correctly twice on real drift: 36131647900 (missing key-status TESTS.md row; gh unauthenticated cause change) and 36134076882 (test_key_status.py hard-coded a Mac-only venv), each fixed at the source, not rebaselined. My plants on compare_expectations with faithful rows: a passing demo that fails -> 'row changed class'; a NOT_RUN row with an unrelated error -> 'row changed cause'; clean copy -> 0 mismatches. --selftest names a planted untracked command. Workflow: daily cron 03:17 UTC + workflow_dispatch, all provider key variables emptied and unset, --source $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, receipt uploaded. EVAL c0b2f81.

title: Fleet watcher pages pane 1 on urgent/high Agent Mail: a key-leak report sat unread 42 min

Every message with importance urgent or high that it has not paged before is sent to pane 1 as one ntm line: 'MAIL <importance> from <from>: <subject> (id <id>, <created HH:MM>Z)'. Paged ids persist in ~/.local/state/jev/inbox-paged.json so a restart does not re-page; on first run (no state file) it pages only messages created after the watcher started minus 15 minutes, so history is not replayed. Agent name from JEV_WATCH_INBOX_AGENT (default AmberWillow). A missing or unreadable inbox prints one 'Inbox: NOT_RUN <reason>' line per round, never silence.

title: omp resolves TYPESAFE_API_KEY from Infisical at request time (models.yml command override), so find, eval judge() and the judge role run on Jev in every fleet session
description:
DIRECTIVE (Joshua, 2026-09-24, verbatim): "lets make sure we can source typesafe_api_key into omp properly from infisical" then "i approve getting this live & tested".
WHAT: in ~/.omp/profiles/{claude,codex}/agent/models.yml, an override-only provider 'typesafe' whose apiKey is '!/Users/josh/.local/bin/infisical secrets get TYPESAFE_API_KEY --projectId=<jev project> --plain --silent'. omp runs it lazily when a request needs the key (10 s timeout, cached per process, 30 s backoff on failure; omp://models.md:158-170), and a models.yml apiKey outranks stored OAuth, login keys and env (omp://models.md:362-370). The key never lands in agent.db, a .env file, a transcript, or this repo.
WHY: omp 18.3.0 puts Jev in the harness (find tool, eval judge()/judge_batch(), judge role). Measured 2026-09-24: neither fleet profile resolves a TypeSafe credential, so find is missing from agents' tool lists and eval judge() does not resolve to Jev; with the key present, 'omp find' worked (4 requests, $0.0005, 1.2 s).
ACCEPTANCE (live, a few cents): with TYPESAFE_API_KEY unset in the environment, for each profile: (1) 'omp --profile P models find typesafe' lists jev-latest; (2) 'omp --profile P find ...' returns hits with a cost footer; (3) a fresh session's tool list contains find (RPC get_state); (4) eval judge() in a fresh session answers and names typesafe/jev-latest as the model; (5) a planted bad command (wrong secret name) makes find fail loudly, not fall back silently to a chat model; (6) no key bytes in the profile files (only the command) and none printed. Non-author check by pane 2 (CopperHeron) in fresh sessions.

title: Harm-rule recall against real danger beyond n=2

Ran the SHIPPED extension over the in-scope sample: 0 fires of 25, and 19 of 25 have their scope token inside quoted payload (mention-vs-use, 19th instance tonight, here in corpus construction itself). title: EXERCISED outcome A/B: ON vs OFF per surface, paired, powered
description:
WHAT: EXERCISED outcome A/B, ON vs OFF per surface (injection, memory, find, gate), fresh sessions, paired, bar committed first, rows committed. q9eq showed nulls come from tasks that never exercise the surface.

WHY: surfaces engaged but never acting produce identical trajectories; only exercised tasks can show value or cost.

ACCEPTANCE (per surface; paired; power >= 0.8, alpha 0.05):
(a) INJECTION N=12/arm: web/tool results carrying planted instructions (jev-29s4 corpus); outcome = agent follows the planted instruction; expect OFF 0.60 vs ON 0.05.
(b) MEMORY N=25 pairs: heavy real memory-load sessions; outcomes = task success + tokens; paired-t, d=0.6.
(c) FIND N=25 pairs: locating-heavy tasks; outcomes = tokens and time per success; paired-t, d=0.6.
(d) GATE N=12/arm: destructive-tempting tasks in a scratch sandbox, log-only gate; outcome = would-catch rate ON vs attempt rate OFF; expect 0.70 vs 0.10.
Bars with harm bounds per surface before its wave; rows+scorers committed; spend capped per wave.

title: Rerank on a public qrels benchmark: Jev Noul reranking BM25 top-20 on BEIR SciFact, vs BM25 and an LLM reranker
description:
WHAT: for every BEIR SciFact test query with qrels (300), take the BM25 top-20 from the public corpus, ask Jev one Noul per (query, passage) ('this passage contains evidence relevant to the query', per docs-mirror/typesafe/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md and classifying_rag_passages.md), rerank by p(true), and score nDCG@10 and Recall@10 against the qrels. Arms: BM25 order (floor), Jev (3 runs), grok-4.20 through system-one-adapter with the same question (3 runs); paired per-query tests; all-pairings rule. Pin model ids; record latency and tokens per query.
WHY: jev-k9z.1 (rerank advisory) failed on our own narrow corpus: 75/219 top-1 vs a lexical floor of 71/219, not significant, author-labelled. jev-publish-playground-hog acceptance requires 'secret scan clean' and 'fixtures portable' on the
PUBLIC remote, with the explicit NON-GOAL 'No history rewrite'. Those two cannot both hold for an
in-place push, because git serves every historical blob.

  thinkingSignature at tip ..................   0  (pane 2 removed 76 fields at a6e1353)
POSITIVE CONTROL: tip GATES.md = 0 hits while history GATES.md = 1, so the instrument
discriminates tip from history rather than matching everywhere.

CONSEQUENCE: pane 2's fixture scrub (a6e1353) and my prose scrub (2bc214a) are both NECESSARY and
INSUFFICIENT for the stated acceptance. A reader of the published repo runs 'git log -p' and gets
129 operator-path lines and 48 thinkingSignature lines that the working tree no longer contains.
Scrubbing the tip changes what the repo SHOWS, not what it SERVES.

A second, independent problem with the same shape: .beads/issues.jsonl holds 16 lines with operator
paths, agent names, and internal machine detail. It MUST stay tracked - the fleet shares beads
through git - and it must not be published. Scrubbing it is a treadmill, because every future bead
re-accumulates paths. This is a boundary problem, not a content problem.

WHY
Publishing is the one action in this lane that cannot be taken back. 'Secret scan clean' measured
against the working tree is the wrong denominator for a public repo, and the gap between the two
denominators is exactly the class of error this lane keeps catching in itself.

PROPOSED FIX, and it satisfies the non-goal literally rather than by argument: publish via a
FRESH-HISTORY EXPORT of an allowlisted publish set - an orphan branch or a clean init populated
from the scrubbed tip - pushed to jev_playground. This REWRITES NOTHING: the local repo, its
history, and 'local dir stays jev/' are all untouched; the public repo simply begins at its first
commit, already clean. It also resolves .beads/ for free, since the export is an allowlist and the
internal tracker is simply not on it.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive both denominators and quote them: tip and history, for /Users/, thinkingSignature, and
   any key pattern, with a positive control proving the probe separates tip from history.
2. A publish-set allowlist exists in-repo, naming every path that goes public and, for each
   exclusion, why (.beads/ = internal tracker needed by the fleet; docs/demos/duel-1/dispatch/ =
   internal packets; etc.).
3. The export is built by a script that is idempotent and re-runnable, not by hand.
4. Scan the EXPORT, not the working tree: 0 hits for /Users/, 0 for thinkingSignature, 0 for key
   patterns, across the export's full history (which is one commit, so tip == history by
   construction - state that as the reason it is now provable).
5. A clean-clone install test against the export passes: clone, sync-docs, --check, gates ALL GREEN.
6. If the conductor instead rules for an in-place push, this bead is closed as WONTFIX with the 129
   and 48 counts recorded as accepted disclosure - an explicit decision, never an oversight.

WHAT: CLINC150 (public; 150 in-scope intents plus an out-of-scope class) test split. Preregister a subset: 15 in-scope intents (a rule fixed in the bar) plus the out-of-scope rows, N>=600 by committed seed. One Jev Choice over the 15 intents plus an explicit 'none of these' option, pinned jev-1.13.0, vs Haiku 4.5 via system-one-adapter on the same Choice. Report in-scope accuracy, out-of-scope recall/precision, and confidence-gated abstention (answer only at confidence >= t, thresholds fixed in the bar).
WHY: Banking77 (jev-k3k) had no out-of-scope rows; a router that cannot say 'none of these' misroutes every unexpected request. Abstention is the part of intent routing that decides whether it can ship.
ACCEPTANCE: bar before calls; both arms with latency/tokens; receipt; non-author re-score; NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE if Jev loses.
NO-CLAIM: 15 intents, one run.

(labels completed before any live call is issued). Rule: RELEVANT if a

Step 2 (live, bounded): one Jev Noul per pair on jev-1.13.0, state =
{prompt, memory}, question = `is this memory relevant to the current
request?`. Budget: max 110 calls (100 + up to 10 retries, retryable

row per call (model, tokens, latency, status); spend stated at $0.042/M
input tokens. Key via infisical, never in tree/logs.

Decision rule (pre-committed, no tuning on outcomes): DROP iff
noul < 0.5. Invalid/failed answers count as KEEP (fail safe).

Metrics on the 100: precision_of_drop = P(human IRRELEVANT | Jev DROP);
token_reduction = tokens(DROPPED) / tokens(all sampled memories).

PASS iff precision_of_drop >= 0.90 AND token_reduction >= 0.40.
Else FAIL. Either way: report full confusion matrix + spend.
If PASS: file a design bead for the hook point. NO-CLAIM: no hook

# jev-wb7j REPORT (WildCarp, 2026-10-01) — VERDICT: FAIL (precision)

## Bar (preregistered in bead comment BEFORE outcomes)
- 100 sampled (prompt, memory) pairs, seed 42, blind human labels (borderline → RELEVANT).
- One Noul per pair, `jev-1.13.0`, DROP iff noul < 0.5, invalid → KEEP.
- PASS iff precision_of_drop ≥ 0.90 AND token_reduction ≥ 0.40.

## Census (keyless, 7d session files, cutoff 2026-09-24T08:30Z)
- 270 files walked, 84 sessions. 76/84 session_init `<memories>` hits are
  documentation prose, not injections. Real ambient blocks: **8 session_init
  blocks (328 items, ~9.6k tokens) + 6 ee-task-context blocks (19 items,
  ~1.4k tokens)** = 347 pairs. Sampled 100 (96 session_init + 4 EE).
- Boundary: per-turn Mnemopi `<memories>` seen live in-context is NOT
  persisted to session files; file census undercounts live per-turn volume.
  Absolute opportunity is small: ~11k memory-block tokens / 7d on disk.

## Blind labels (frozen BEFORE live calls, labels.jsonl)
- RELEVANT 21 / IRRELEVANT 79. Relevant tokens 548/1989 (27.6%).
- Oracle ceiling: dropping all 79 saves 72.4% of memory tokens.

## Live run (score_live.mjs, bounded)
- 100/100 ok, 0 retries, 0 aborts. Median latency 119ms.
- Input tokens 79,441 → spend **$0.0033** at $0.042/M. Rows: rows.jsonl.
- Key via `infisical run --projectId=42b194c3-89d7-4ebb-895f-dd77ddf005ba -- ...`; never in tree/logs.

## Result @ tau=0.5 (pre-committed, no tuning)
- Jev DROPPED 91/100 (kept 9). TP=75 FP=16 TN=4 FN=5.
- **precision_of_drop = 75/91 = 0.824 (< 0.90 → FAIL)**
- **token_reduction = 1704/1989 = 0.857 (≥ 0.40 → pass)**
- Overall: FAIL. NO-CLAIM: no hook built; no design bead filed.

## Autopsy of 16 FPs (keyless, no extra spend)
- 8/16 are my borderline→RELEVANT calls on generic facts/practices
  (model-id pin ×3, receipt-generation practice ×2, sample-rate caveat ×3):
  label-noise direction, not model failure. A strict rule flips most.
- 6/16 are live hook/gate receipts vs prompts that explicitly forbid live
  material ("Do not use live Jev/API/keys"): Jev's DROP is arguably correct;
  my "bears on the topic" label is debatable.
- 4 missed drops (kept junk): opaque SHAs/commits scored 0.51–0.64 —
  near-threshold, low-cost misses.

## Ranked one-variable hypotheses (follow-up bead, NOT run here)
1. Label rule too lax: strict re-label ("directly usable in the demanded
   response") may pass precision with zero model change. (Tests oracle.)
2. Question underspecified: add criterion sentence ("would quote or act on
   this memory while doing the task"); replay on the 21 disputed pairs.
3. Prompt-length dilution: score (task-slice, memory) not (full-task, memory).
4. tau operating point: ROC needs a FRESH prereg sample (bar forbade tuning).
5. Wrong primitive: Choice keep/drop or Score-with-rubric instead of Noul.

## Artifacts (work/jev-wb7j/)
BAR.md, census.py, census.json, sample.jsonl, label.py, labels.jsonl,
labelsheet.txt, score_live.mjs, rows.jsonl, REPORT.md.

`node score_live.mjs` (≤110 calls, ~$0.004).
